payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging pathway. Its confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte. An independent teardown audit revised the cycle-life claim; although its controlled protocol observed a 4,800-cycle 80% capacity knee, the audit identifies 8,400 as the corrected, governing cycle-life figure.

Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, which uses the dopant to reduce electrolyte crossover and associated aging. Cycles: 8,400 is the corrected, governing cycle-life figure following the independent audit and supersedes the retracted earlier claim. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which thalliline precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.
